rationale: The workflow already satisfies the dependency-caching optimization (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) via `cache: npm` in the setup-node step, so no cache needs to be added. No matrix exists, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply. The trigger is workflow_dispatch only and the job creates branches, commits, and pull requests (release-like work), so P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated. Path-based change filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) is not meaningful for a manual dispatch with no push/pull_request trigger. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT requires representative successful-duration history, but the repository CI history contains only two runs and both failed, so no safe timeout budget can be established; an arbitrary limit risks failing valid slow dependency-update/lint/test/build runs, which is the pattern's stated contraindication. No other pattern's preconditions are met for this workflow.
